title: NOx Exceedence - Deactivation of EGR
shortDescription: PCM detected: nox exceedence - deactivation of egr fault triggering NOx-related torque limit.
fullDescription:
This DTC indicates nox exceedence - deactivation of egr fault triggering NOx-related torque limit. The PCM monitors related signals against learned thresholds and stores the code when the fault matures.

On diesel vehicles this typically results in regulated torque derate and a 'driver inducement' countdown until the underlying SCR/DEF fault is corrected. Continued operation will lead to a no-restart condition.
safetyImpact: Vehicle will enter limp mode and may refuse to restart after derate countdown expires.

causes.cause: Faulty NOx sensor (upstream or downstream of SCR)

fixSteps.title: Scan and capture freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Read all stored and pending codes; record freeze-frame data.

fixSteps.title: Visual inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect SCR catalyst, NOx sensors, DEF doser, DEF supply lines wiring, connectors, and related components for damage.

fixSteps.title: Electrical/functional test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify reference, ground, and signal at the affected connector with engine running; perform manufacturer-specific actuator/monitor test.

fixSteps.title: Replace component or perform service procedure
fixSteps.instruction: If circuit checks pass, replace the suspect component or perform required regen/relearn and clear codes.

faq.a: Yes for short distances if engine runs normally; otherwise flatbed.
No - sensor or component replacement is typically required.

title: Reductant Quality Performance
shortDescription: PCM detected: reductant quality performance - reductant (DEF) quality fault.
fullDescription:
This DTC indicates reductant quality performance - reductant (DEF) quality fault. The PCM monitors related signals against learned thresholds and stores the code when the fault matures.

If DEF concentration is outside spec or contaminated, the SCR cannot reduce NOx and emissions monitors will fail. Refill or drain/refill of the DEF tank with fresh fluid is normally required.
safetyImpact: Will progress to inducement and reduced power.

causes.cause: Wrong fluid (water/diesel) added to DEF tank

title: NOx Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 2
shortDescription: PCM detected: nox sensor circuit bank 1 sensor 2 fault detected by PCM.
fullDescription:
This DTC indicates nox sensor circuit bank 1 sensor 2 fault detected by PCM. The PCM monitors related signals against learned thresholds and stores the code when the fault matures.

Bank 1 Sensor 2 is the downstream NOx sensor used to verify SCR conversion efficiency. Faults here typically force the SCR closed-loop strategy open and trigger NOx exceedence codes.
safetyImpact: Vehicle remains drivable but emissions are non-compliant.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency
shortDescription: PCM detected: diesel particulate filter regeneration frequency fault.
fullDescription:
This DTC indicates diesel particulate filter regeneration frequency fault. The PCM monitors related signals against learned thresholds and stores the code when the fault matures.

DPF differential pressure (delta-P) is monitored to schedule active regeneration. Faults here can either allow soot overload or force constant regen, both of which damage the DPF substrate over time.
safetyImpact: Risk of clogged DPF and limp mode if ignored.

causes.cause: DPF saturated with soot or ash

title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: PCM detected: reductant tank temperature sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
This DTC indicates reductant tank temperature sensor circuit fault. The PCM monitors related signals against learned thresholds and stores the code when the fault matures.

DEF freezes at -11C, so the system relies on temperature sensors to control tank and line heaters. A failed sensor can leave the system unable to thaw or can falsely trigger heater overheating.
safetyImpact: May prevent SCR operation in cold weather.

DEF freezes at -11C, so the system relies on temperature sensors to control tank and line heaters. A failed sensor can leave the system unable to thaw or can falsely trigger heater overheating.
safetyImpact: May prevent SCR operation in cold weather.

fixSteps.title: Scan and capture freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Read all stored and pending codes; record freeze-frame data.

fixSteps.title: Visual inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect DEF temperature sensor, harness wiring, connectors, and related components for damage.

fixSteps.title: Electrical/functional test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify reference, ground, and signal at the affected connector with engine running; perform manufacturer-specific actuator/monitor test.

fixSteps.title: Replace component or perform service procedure
fixSteps.instruction: If circuit checks pass, replace the suspect component or perform required regen/relearn and clear codes.

faq.a: Yes for short distances if engine runs normally; otherwise flatbed.
No - sensor or component replacement is typically required.

title: Reductant Tank Heater 'A' Control Circuit/Open
shortDescription: PCM detected: reductant tank heater 'a' control circuit/open fault.
fullDescription:
This DTC indicates reductant tank heater 'a' control circuit/open fault. The PCM monitors related signals against learned thresholds and stores the code when the fault matures.

DEF heaters keep urea liquid in cold ambient temperatures. A heater fault prevents SCR operation in freezing conditions and triggers the inducement timer.
safetyImpact: Cold-weather operation may cause derate.
